# `silk/concurrency/execution_storage`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Storage for the private execution frames that the compiler makes.

## When to use
The compiler and the runtime use this module through its C exports. Application code does not
call it.

## Details
Each `ExecutionStorage` state owns its limit, its accounting and its frames. There is no
shared counter and no environment lookup. A state is a stack: frames are carved one after
another from segments, and released in reverse order, so a callee's frame sits right after its
caller's and costs no allocation of its own. The first segment comes with the state; a frame
that does not fit starts a segment twice the size of the last, which stays for reuse once it
empties. Segments use the declared allocator of the selected target.

## Errors
`ExecutionStorage.make` fails with `OutOfMemoryError`. `ExecutionStorage.acquire` returns
null when a frame does not fit in the limit or cannot be allocated.

## Gotchas
- Raw frame access is unsafe. A frame is valid only until it is released or its state is
  destroyed.
- Frames are released last first; releasing any other frame corrupts the state.
- One state needs exclusive use. Independent states can use a concurrent host allocator.
